name: MIC811TUY-TR
title: MIC811/MIC812 microprocessor reset circuits in 4-pin SOT-143
summary: A one-channel supply supervisor for 3 V, 3.3 V and 5 V microprocessor systems. It holds its reset output asserted while VCC sits below a factory-set threshold, or while the manual reset input /MR is low, and for at least 140 ms after both conditions clear. The output is push-pull, so it needs no pull-up: the MIC811 drives an active-low /RESET, the MIC812 an active-high RESET. Six thresholds from 2.63 V to 4.63 V; MIC811TUY is the active-low part with the 3.08 V threshold.
key_figures: 3.00 V min, 3.08 V typ, 3.15 V max over -40 °C to +85 °C
5 µA typ; 10 µA max (R/S/T), 15 µA max (L/M/J)

pins.name: /RESET
pins.function: Active-low push-pull reset output. Pulled low when VCC drops under the reset threshold; held low until VCC has been above the threshold for one reset timeout period (140 ms min.).

pins.name: /MR
pins.function: Manual reset, active low, with an internal pull-up. While it is low the reset output stays asserted, and it stays asserted for one reset timeout (140 ms min.) after /MR returns high. A switch to ground or a CMOS or TTL logic output may drive it; leave it open when not used.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply input, and the voltage that is monitored.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Active-high push-pull reset output. Driven high when VCC drops under the reset threshold; held high until VCC has been above the threshold for one reset timeout period (140 ms min.).

pins.name: /MR
pins.function: Manual reset, active low, with an internal pull-up. While it is low the reset output stays asserted, and it stays asserted for one reset timeout (140 ms min.) after /MR returns high. A switch to ground or a CMOS or TTL logic output may drive it; leave it open when not used.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The MIC811 and a microprocessor run from one VCC rail and share ground. The supervisor's /RESET output drives the processor's /RESET input directly, with no pull-up since the output is push-pull. A push-button from /MR to ground gives a manual reset.

circuits.title: Reset valid to VCC = 0V
circuits.description: The same supervisor-to-processor connection with a 100 kΩ resistor from the /RESET line to ground, so the line is held low as VCC falls all the way to 0 V. /MR is left open.

operation.text: Reset is asserted whenever VCC is under VTH and is released 140 ms (minimum) after VCC has risen back above VTH. The output stays valid with VCC as low as 1 V.
A comparator sets VCC against an internal reset threshold; its output and the /MR input both feed a reset generator, which drives pin 2.

Pulling /MR low asserts reset after about 0.5 µs; the low pulse must last at least 10 µs, and pulses of about 100 ns or shorter are ignored. Reset stays asserted for one timeout after /MR goes high again. An internal pull-up of 10 kΩ to 30 kΩ holds /MR high when it is left open.
Both a low pulse on /MR and a dip of VCC under VTH bring /RESET low at once; in each case /RESET goes high again tRST after the cause has gone (after /MR rises, or after VCC climbs back through VTH).
Brief negative-going glitches of VCC under the threshold are largely tolerated: typically a 125 mV dip lasting 20 µs or less causes no reset.

operation.topic: Output held low down to 0 V
operation.text: A 100 kΩ resistor from /RESET to ground is the recommended way to keep the output low with VCC all the way down to 0 V. The resistor is sized so that it loads the output only lightly yet still pulls down stray leakage.
Where the processor's reset pin can also drive, place a 4.7 kΩ resistor in series between the MIC811/812 output and that pin.
The output is push-pull and needs no pull-up resistor. An open-drain version of this supervisor is the MIC6315.
